value.rationale: The triangular graphs are a canonical Johnson/line-graph family in which the adjacent five-point four-cut case is known. For six points the homology occupies two nonadjacent degrees 8 and 10 within a pure 10-complex, giving a substantive and coefficient-robust obstruction to shellability and Cohen–Macaulayness. Both exact integral ranks and torsion freeness are nontrivial and reproducible, with plausible use as an initial classification boundary.
